I often come across interesting resources, but they tend to get lost among my bookmarks. This post is a living collection of the ones I want to revisit, shared in case they are useful to others too.

## Programming

### Python

- [Calmcode](https://calmcode.io/) — Short, practical video courses on Python, data tools, and software development.

### Julia

- [Julia's learning hub](https://julialang.org/learning/) — The official collection of courses, tutorials, books, and exercises for getting started with the language.

## Software development

- [The Missing Semester of Your CS Education](https://missing.csail.mit.edu/) — An MIT course on the practical tools that complement a computer science education: the shell, editors, Git, debugging, and code quality.
- [The Modern Software Developer](https://themodernsoftware.dev/) — Stanford's CS146S course on AI-native software development, including coding agents, MCP, agent skills, specification-driven development, and evaluation.

## Data Science

- [Made with ML](https://madewithml.com/) — An end-to-end course on developing and deploying machine-learning applications.
- [Aprende con Alf](https://aprendeconalf.es/) *(in Spanish)* — A little outdated in places, but still a useful collection of programming, statistics, and machine-learning tutorials.
- [Machine Learning from Scratch](https://dafriedman97.github.io/mlbook/content/introduction.html) — A classic resource for understanding machine-learning algorithms by deriving and implementing them from scratch.

### People Analytics

- [Fundamentals of People Analytics: With Applications in R](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-28674-2) — An introduction to the field with hands-on examples.
- [People Analytics: Regression Modelling](https://peopleanalytics-regression-book.org/) — A practical guide to regression modelling in a people-analytics context.
- [Organizational Network Analysis](https://ona-book.org/) — Graph and network methods applied to people analytics.

### Finance

- [Tidy Finance with Python](https://www.tidy-finance.org/python/) — A must-read for applying reproducible data-science workflows to financial research.

## Deep Learning

Foundational books and visual aids worth knowing:

- [Deep Learning](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/) — A comprehensive reference for the mathematical and conceptual foundations of the field.
- [Understanding Deep Learning](https://udlbook.github.io/udlbook/) — A modern, accessible textbook with accompanying figures and notebooks.
- [Stanford's machine-learning cheatsheets](https://stanford.edu/~shervine/teaching/) — Concise summaries of machine-learning and deep-learning concepts.
- [ML Visualized](https://ml-visualized.com/) — Visual explanations that help build intuition for machine-learning concepts.

### Large language models

I highly recommend [Sebastian Raschka's magazine](https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/) for deep dives into concepts and architectures. Other useful resources include:

- [Foundations of Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.09223) — A survey of the core ideas behind modern LLMs.
- [Applied LLMs](https://applied-llms.org/) — A collection of practical resources for building with LLMs.
- [How to Scale Your Model](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/) — A systems-oriented guide to scaling machine-learning models.
- [BentoML's LLM inference guide](https://bentoml.com/llm/) — An introduction to inference concepts and optimization.
- [Anthropic Academy](https://www.anthropic.com/learn) — Courses on working with Claude and building with Anthropic's tools.
- [Hands-On Large Language Models](https://github.com/HandsOnLLM/Hands-On-Large-Language-Models) — Code and exercises accompanying the book.
